**Finding: LICENSE — compliant (preferred level).**

The grant clauses satisfy every preferred element without amendment:

- **Affiliates and contractors** — § 13.1 grants the subscription access right directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," so no written-notice add-on mechanic is required; § 13.2 likewise names Affiliates and permits contractors to support the material.
- **Perpetual / irrevocable paid-up licence** — § 13.2 gives a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, and § 14.3 pulls Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable into that same § 13.2 licence.
- **Revocation only for uncured material breach** — § 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending except during a material uncured payment or use breach, after notice and a reasonable cure period; nothing in the document makes the licence revocable at Vendor's discretion.
- **Successor transferability** — § 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor tied to an assignment permitted by § 24, and § 24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or M&A successor, so the transfer path is real rather than circular.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not redlined here: § 14.2's "revocable, non-transferable" Deliverable licence sits in tension with this package. That is a Deliverable ownership/licence problem for the IP rule, and flagging it here as well would double-count the same commercial term.
